title: Autoclave operation
summary: Run a sterilization cycle on liquids or biohazard waste without scalding yourself or letting a bottle explode.
hazardsMd: Burn risk: chamber walls and load stay >100 °C after cycle end. Liquid loads can flash-boil if the cycle is wrong. Never run a sealed-cap bottle.
contentUndergrad:
## Why autoclave
Steam at 121 °C and 15 psi for 30 minutes kills the vast majority of microbes, including bacterial spores. The right cycle for the right load is what matters.

steps.title: Prepare the load
steps.instructionMd: For LIQUIDS: use heat-stable bottles, fill ≤ 75%, loosen caps a quarter turn. For WASTE: use a red autoclave bag, leave the mouth cuffed open. Apply autoclave-indicator tape to every item.
steps.safetyNotesMd: Glass bottles with sealed caps will explode. Plastic that's not autoclave-rated will melt.
steps.verificationMd: Every item has indicator tape on the outside. Liquid bottle caps are noticeably loose (not finger-tight).

steps.title: Place in a secondary tray
steps.instructionMd: Set the load inside an autoclave-rated stainless or polypropylene tray. The tray catches any boil-over and keeps the chamber clean.
steps.verificationMd: Tray sits flat with the load inside; the autoclave door will close without contact.

steps.title: Select the right cycle
steps.instructionMd:
Liquids: Liquid cycle, 121 °C, 30 min, slow exhaust.
Waste: Waste/Gravity cycle, 121 °C, 60 min.
Dry goods: Dry cycle, 121 °C, 30 min, fast exhaust.
steps.safetyNotesMd: Running a Dry cycle on bottled liquids triggers boil-over and bottle rupture.
steps.verificationMd: Cycle name on the screen matches the load type. Total time displayed includes ~15-20 min ramp + dwell + exhaust.

steps.title: Start the cycle and wait
steps.instructionMd: Close the door fully (you should hear the gasket seat). Hit Start. Stay nearby for the first 5 min to confirm pressure is rising normally; then leave the cycle to finish.
steps.verificationMd: Pressure gauge climbs steadily during ramp; no leak hiss audible from the door.

steps.title: Unload safely
steps.instructionMd: Wait until the pressure gauge reads zero AND the door pin retracts. Wear heat-rated gloves. Open the door slowly to let residual steam vent away from your face. Move the load to a designated cooling area.
steps.safetyNotesMd: Liquids boil for several minutes after the cycle ends. Do not move bottles until they've cooled below 80 °C; bumping them can trigger flash-boiling.
steps.verificationMd: Indicator tape stripes are dark. Bag/bottle contents look uniformly heated. Logbook entry filled in (date, user, cycle, load contents).
